title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LE0LD_1RB1LA_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LE0LD_1RB1LA_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Unlike most machines of its group, this one is not slow on the right: the head sweeps the whole tape again and again, and the tape grows like a power of the step count (about t0.66: 57,266 cells after 109 steps). Almost all of the tape is one long periodic run: the word 0110 repeated when the head has just reached the left end, the word 1110 when it has just reached the right end. Each sweep turns every word into the other one (the rightward sweep turns 0110 into 1110, the leftward one back). Near the left end sits a short irregular part (0 (110)^32 0 (110)^3 0 110 … around step 2.5·108) that acts as a counter and decides how far the next sweeps go; the width grows in jumps (by 1,621, 3,237, 3,217, 6,473 and 6,477 cells between the turns listed below), which roughly double every second jump.
verdict: The question is open. The machine can halt only from C> 1 0 (proved in Lean); in 20,000,000,000 steps that never happens, and in the first 109 steps C never even reads a 1 followed by a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 57,266 cells have been visited and 28,671 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.069). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From C> 1 0 the machine reaches F on a 0, its halting transition, in one step (halt_ctx, then step_none_iff). F is entered only from C reading a 1, which moves right.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Four shift rules (for example B> (1)^n becomes (0)^n B> in n steps, (110)^n A> 1 becomes A> 1 (110)^n), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the tape then holds 203,768 ones.

claims.title: No near misses
claims.text: In the first 109 steps C read 1 1, 0 0 or 0 1 ahead, never 1 0: every 1 that C reads is followed by another 1.

claims.title: Power-law growth
claims.text: The width grows like t<sup>0.66</sup> (triage fit); the head turns at the ends at the steps listed on the explainer page, with the width jumping by roughly doubling amounts.

claims.title: 60 event rules for every size
claims.text: From an event (E on cell 135) to the next: 8-step events such as E> 0 1 0 0 0 1 → E> 1 1 0 1 1 1, and events that turn a run of 1110 words on the left into 1101 words (8a+28 steps), each proved for every value of its repeat counts.

claims.title: Coverage: 99.7% of the events
claims.text: 2,088,696 events in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, 6,155 not matched by a rule. The events are a small part of the run: most steps are sweeps over the long run, which lie inside uncovered events.

claims.title: C> 1 0 never occurs
claims.text: In 3·109 steps C never has 1 0 ahead.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. C reads a 1 only inside the words 0110/1110 of the long run or in the counter at the left end, and so far always with a 1 after it; a proof would need the rule of the counter and of how far the sweeps reach.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head sweeps a long run of four-cell words back and forth, and between sweeps it works at one cell near the left end; 99.7% of its events there follow rules proved for every size, but the sweeps themselves and what sets their length are not yet a rule. The one way to stop has never come up.

facts.text: Event rules proved in Lean for every size.
Of the 2,088,696 events of 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps follow them.
From it the machine halts (Lean halt_ctx); every halt passes through it (from the table).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.069). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659).
After 109 steps the tape spans 57,266 cells (101 left of the start, 40,215 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A bouncer with a counter

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0, and F is entered only from C reading a 1 (C writes 1 and moves right). So the machine halts exactly from C> 1 0; Lean proves the step (halt_ctx).
What C has ahead of it, counted at every step of the first 109 steps:

0 0 014,351999,936,638

C never reads a 1 followed by a 0. In the long run C reads the 1s of 0110/1110 from the left, so a 1 always follows; the counter at the left end is the only place where something else could happen.

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: A description of the sweeps as a rule on (counter, length of the run), from which one would read that C never meets 1 0. The long run is crossed by shift rules (proved in lean/Rules.lean), so the counter at the left end is the missing piece.

summary: A bouncer with a counter: sweeps turn a long run of 0110 into 1110 and back, and near the left end the head works at one cell (E on cell 135); 60 event rules there proved for all sizes cover 99.7% of 2.1·10^6 events in 3·10^9 steps; C> 1 0 (from it the machine halts) never occurs.
family: sweeping bouncer over 0110/1110, with a counter
